contraindications.reason: Thiazide diuretics are ineffective and may worsen glucose tolerance in eGFR <30 mL/min; contraindicated in CKD 5

contraindications.reason: NSAIDs are contraindicated in CKD 5 due to risk of further renal impairment and fluid retention
contraindications.alternative: Paracetamol up to 3 g/day or topical NSAID if needed

treatment_summary: Continue ACE‑I (lisinopril) and CCB (amlodipine) for hypertension, add a low‑dose loop diuretic (furosemide) because thiazides are ineffective at eGFR 15 mL/min, start atorvastatin for cardiovascular risk reduction, and introduce semaglutide for obesity and pre‑diabetes. Discontinue hydrochlorothiazide and naproxen due to CKD‑5 contraindications and replace naproxen with paracetamol for pain. Monitor BP, renal function, electrolytes, lipids, liver enzymes, weight and HbA1c per NICE NG136, CG181 and PH38. Provide lifestyle advice (diet, exercise, smoking cessation) and arrange necessary labs and QRISK calculation before finalising doses.
